answer: To resist sybils, agents maintain a public Merkle orchard of identity commitments. A new agent posts a cipher (hash of a secret seed) into the orchard and must solve a sequential VDF of 2^20 steps before opening any inlet for transactions or votes. The VDF forces serial computation that parallel hardware cannot accelerate, so an attacker forging 1000 identities spends 1000 times the wall-clock time of one honest agent, plus the opportunity cost of locked capital during the delay. This makes mass fabrication unprofitable relative to honest participation.
